content.text: {"answer":"The trigger was a security gap: with the original design, any authenticated user obtained the org-wide FLY_API_TOKEN via the CLI, which meant that user had credentials for every machine in the Fly org (d2). The builder flagged this as unacceptable once a second user could exist ('any authenticated user gets credentials for every machine in the org. That must end before a second user exists.'). The fix was to have the Worker keep the org admin token server-side and instead mint a per-app, 1-hour-expiring deploy token (via createLimitedAccessToken) that is the only Fly credential ever sent to the CLI (d2; packages/control-plane/src/fly.js lines 1-2, 48-56). This required using the Fly user auth token as the worker's own credential, since only user tokens can mint limited-access tokens (d5).","citations":[{"kind":"decision","decision_id":"d2"},{"kind":"message","message_id":"m1812"},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":1,"end_line":2},{"kind":"code","path":"packages/control-plane/src/fly.js","start_line":48,"end_line":56},{"kind":"decision","decision_id":"d5"}]}
